query: Which material can be used for enhance glass-forming ability, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding alkali metals to silica-based glass compositions will enhance their glass-forming ability.
generation.material_initial_state: Silica-based glass without alkali metal additives.
generation.intervention: Incorporation of alkali metal oxides (e.g., Na2O, K2O) into the glass composition.
generation.conditions: Controlled melting and cooling processes to form glass from the modified composition.
generation.structural_mediator: Altered glass network structure due to the introduction of alkali metal ions.
generation.mechanism: Alkali metal ions disrupt the silica network, reducing the viscosity and facilitating the formation of a glassy state during cooling.
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased glass-forming ability, evidenced by a lower melting temperature and improved glass transition temperature.
generation.baseline: Standard silica glass without alkali metal additives.
generation.boundary: Effects may vary with different types and amounts of alkali metals used.
generation.uncertainty: The exact extent of enhancement in glass-forming ability is uncertain and may depend on specific compositions and processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare multiple glass samples with varying concentrations of alkali metal oxides and a control sample without them. Melt and cool each sample under identical conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples with alkali metal additives do not show a statistically significant reduction in melting temperature or viscosity compared to the control, the hypothesis is falsified.
